modules.name: shared/types
owns: LeaveType enum (annual | sick | emergency | unpaid | maternity | paternity)
LeaveStatus enum (DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED)
AuditAction enum (CREATE | UPDATE | DELETE | APPROVE | REJECT)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Shared types & enums
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency foundation. Every downstream module imports these. Must exist first.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeavePolicy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared types. LeaveService needs policy validation before it can process requests.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — LeaveBalance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared types. LeaveService needs balance checks before approving requests.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — LeaveRequest module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared types. Core entity and persistence for leave requests.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Audit module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared types. Required by GP-002: every state change must write an audit record.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6 — Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared types. LeaveService fires notifications on state transitions.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7 — LeaveService & API surface
recommended_phases.rationale: Orchestrator that wires all inner modules together. Depends on all prior phases. Includes controller, routes, and RBAC guards.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (LeaveController, LeaveRoutes), application (LeaveService orchestrating across inner modules), domain (LeaveRequest, Balance, LeavePolicy entities + their repository interfaces), infrastructure (repository implementations, PostgreSQL/Knex). Dependencies flow inward: LeaveRoutes → LeaveController → LeaveService → {LeaveRequestRepo, LeaveBalanceRepo, LeavePolicyRepo, AuditService, NotificationService}. All inner modules (leave-request, leave-balance, leave-policy, audit, notification) depend only on src/shared/types/. The LeaveService is the sole orchestrator — no inner module calls another inner module. Audit (GP-002) and RBAC (GP-005) are enforced at the LeaveService and route-guard levels respectively.

open_questions.question: Balance deduction semantics: when deductBalance is called, should it (a) increment usedDays AND decrement remainingDays atomically, or (b) only decrement remainingDays and let a separate recalculateRemainingDays reconcile usedDays later? The Balance entity tracks both fields independently.
open_questions.impact: Affects deductBalance, restoreBalance, and recalculateRemainingDays implementations. Inconsistent semantics across these methods would produce BR-001 violations where sibling methods disagree on the same derived value.
candidate_options: Option A: Atomic dual-update — deductBalance always increments usedDays and decrements remainingDays in one transaction; restoreBalance reverses both.
Option B: Single-field — deductBalance only decrements remainingDays; usedDays is derived via recalculateRemainingDays (totalEntitlement - remainingDays) on read.

auth_contract: Authenticated request shape: request.user = { id: string; role: UserRole }. UserRole enum: 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. Identity obtained via JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware (populates request.user). RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...) route-level guard — never inline in handlers. Endpoint access: submitLeaveRequest → employee; approveLeaveRequest / rejectLeaveRequest → manager; getPendingLeaveRequestsForManager → manager; getLeaveBalance / getAllLeaveBalances → employee (own) or manager/hr_admin (any); cancelLeaveRequest → employee (own) or hr_admin.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string; details?: unknown }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 ({ error: "Validation failed", code: "VALIDATION_ERROR", details: [...] }). Authentication failure → HTTP 401 ({ error: "Unauthorized", code: "AUTH_REQUIRED" }). Authorization failure → HTTP 403 ({ error: "Forbidden", code: "INSUFFICIENT_ROLE" }). Not found → HTTP 404 ({ error: "Leave request not found", code: "NOT_FOUND" }). Business rule violation (e.g. insufficient balance, inactive policy) → HTTP 409 ({ error: "...", code: "BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION" }).
